items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: I went to Copacabana club because Anita O’Day was one of my favorite white singers. She sat at the bar and cried.

ctx.x: And being a poet, have you set any of your poems to melodies?

Yes, yes. I just did “Lonely Woman” by Ornette Coleman. And Ornette never liked the lyrics. They were done by a poet he never got introduced to, by a woman. And he said, “That’s not what my song is about.” And Ornette and me, we just keep talking together. And so I called him and said, “Ornette, can I write some lyrics for ‘Lonely Woman’ and come down and show them to you and then record it? He said, “You just write it, you don’t have to come down, record it and bring me the recording.” Because he knows my…

musicians in this country, it’s Ornette is like a guru to us. He’s like a guru. He kept us. We wanted to leave the second week we came here. Because when you come from Europe all these musicians they come from here are superstars there. They are honored. People go to the concerts. People put extra dress on, extra suit. And then you come over here. The first experience was a very famous musician, I don’t want to mention his name, a saxophone player, came over and asked Karl for a few dollars so he can buy a new…
